lesson_title: Mapwork Paper Practice Run: A Full Practice Map, Marked Step by Step
hook_text: Five marks for five lines of working. Watch a gradient question get banked one step at a time.
clip_script: Calculate the average gradient between point A, where the path crosses the one thousand two hundred and sixty metre contour, and the trigonometrical beacon at B on Uitkyk. Step one, vertical interval: one thousand five hundred and twelve comma six minus one thousand two hundred and sixty — two hundred and fifty-two comma six metres. Step two, horizontal equivalent: four comma two centimetres on the map, at one to fifty thousand that is two thousand one hundred metres. Step three, substitute and divide: one in eight comma three. The marking pays a mark for each step — the interval, the measurement, the equivalent, the substitution, the ratio — and even allows a millimetre of ruler difference. Working shown, five out of five.
visual_style: Answer page filling line by line over a sketched contour slope rising to a beacon: each written step stamps +1 as it lands, ending on 5/5 with the accepted range 1:8,1 to 1:8,5 shown as a green band.
pacing: Methodical beats, one per calculation step, with a quick payoff montage of the five marks landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and work the rest of the Kransfontein map yourself.
